meta.exam_title: Written Exam No. 3 – Living and studying in a globalized world

criteria.short: Fasst das Ausmaß der Plastikverschmutzung der Meere zusammen
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling fasst das Ausmaß der Plastikverschmutzung der Meere zusammen, etwa:
bullets: explains that an enormous amount of plastic waste enters the oceans every year, comparable to a vast area covered ankle-deep in rubbish
refers to the almost 19 billion pounds of plastic waste estimated to reach the oceans annually
points out that this amount is expected to double within less than a decade if nothing changes
mentions the wide range of single-use plastic items involved, from bottles and bags to straws and packaging

criteria.short: Stellt die Ursachen und Quellen der Verschmutzung dar
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling stellt die Ursachen und Quellen der Verschmutzung dar, etwa:
bullets: explains that single-use packaging is identified as the main source of ocean litter
describes how everyday items such as bags, bottles or wrappers travel via streams and drains into rivers and eventually the sea
notes that the cheapness and disposability of plastic are named as reasons for its widespread and careless use

criteria.short: Erklärt die Auswirkungen der Plastikverschmutzung auf Tiere und Menschen
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling erklärt die Auswirkungen der Plastikverschmutzung auf Tiere und Menschen, etwa:
bullets: outlines that hundreds of animal species are affected, with many marine animals mistaking plastic for food
gives examples of specific animals harmed or killed by ingesting plastic, including turtles, whales and seabirds
points out that the proportion of seabirds affected is expected to rise further in the coming decades
mentions that humans may also be affected indirectly through plastics entering the food chain via seafood, with health risks still uncertain

criteria.short: Fasst die im Artikel dargestellte Rolle des Einzelnen zusammen
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling fasst die im Artikel dargestellte Rolle des Einzelnen zusammen, etwa:
bullets: explains that individuals are described as having an important part to play in reducing the problem
mentions simple everyday actions such as avoiding single-use items or reusing bottles and bags
points out that individual choices are presented as more significant in densely populated areas
summarizes the overall message that collective individual action can make a meaningful difference

criteria.short: Entwickelt eine schlüssige These, die aufzeigt, wie stilistische Mittel, Tonfall, Register und Argumentationslinie zusammenwirken, um die Botschaft der Autorin überzeugend zu vermitteln
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling entwickelt eine schlüssige These, die aufzeigt, wie stilistische Mittel, Tonfall, Register und Argumentationslinie zusammenwirken, um die Botschaft der Autorin überzeugend zu vermitteln, z. B.:
bullets: points out that Mosbergen combines vivid imagery, expert authority and an emotional register to move readers from alarm to a sense of individual responsibility
notes that the shift from urgency ("stem the tide of garbage", l. 9) to empowerment ("your choices can make an impact", l. 42) structures the persuasive strategy
highlights that statistics and expert quotations lend the argument credibility while personal, everyday examples make it relatable
argues that the combination of pathos-driven imagery and logos-based evidence is designed to convince readers across different levels of prior knowledge

criteria.short: Analysiert die von Mosbergen eingesetzten stilistischen Mittel und deren Wirkung
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling analysiert die von Mosbergen eingesetzten stilistischen Mittel und deren Wirkung, z. B.:
bullets: identifies the hyperbolic comparison "an area 34 times the size of Manhattan" (l. 1-2) as a device making an abstract quantity of waste imaginable
points out the direct quotation "We're being overwhelmed by our waste" (l. 1, 6) used as a dramatic opening and closing frame
notes the use of statistics, e.g. "19 billion pounds of garbage" (l. 4), as evidence adding scientific credibility
highlights the appeal to authority through expert quotations by Jambeck (l. 6-9) and Mallos (l. 18)
comments on the emotive imagery of affected wildlife, e.g. "a dead whale beached on Norway's coast had 30 plastic bags in its stomach" (l. 25-26), as a means of evoking pathos

criteria.short: Bestimmt den Tonfall des Textes und dessen Wandel im Textverlauf mithilfe passender Adjektive
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling bestimmt den Tonfall des Textes und dessen Wandel im Textverlauf mithilfe passender Adjektive, z. B.:
bullets: describes the tone in the opening paragraphs as alarming and urgent, reinforced by phrases such as "swiftly... to stem the tide of garbage" (l. 8-9)
points out a more sober, factual undertone when statistics and research findings are presented, e.g. "led the 2015 study that determined this staggering number" (l. 7)
identifies a shift towards a hopeful, empowering tone towards the end, e.g. "it's empowering as a citizen to know that your choices can make an impact" (l. 41-42)
notes subtle undertones of concern for human health in the more cautious phrase "not totally clear" (l. 30)
identifies the overall tonal trajectory as a deliberate move from alarm to encouragement, designed to avoid overwhelming or discouraging the reader

criteria.short: Untersucht das Register des Textes anhand der verwendeten Wortfelder
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling untersucht das Register des Textes anhand der verwendeten Wortfelder, z. B.:
bullets: points out the scientific/academic word field in terms such as "environmental engineer", "study" and "research" (l. 6-7)
identifies more colloquial, everyday phrasing such as "things that may seem mundane" (l. 40) aimed at a general readership
notes the mixture of technical vocabulary ("reproductive problems", l. 32) and accessible explanations suitable for a broad, non-expert audience
comments on the use of direct address and inclusive language ("our waste", l. 6; "all of us", l. 34) to bridge the gap between expert and lay register

criteria.short: Erläutert die Argumentationslinie des Textes
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling erläutert die Argumentationslinie des Textes, z. B.:
bullets: identifies the overall structure as a problem-solution frame, moving from the description of the crisis to a call for individual action
points out that the line of argument is largely one-sided/thetic, building a case for urgent action rather than presenting an antithetic position
notes the concession "the potential risks to human health... are not totally clear" (l. 30) as a brief two-sided element adding balance and credibility
explains how the argument types shift from factual/statistical evidence to an appeal to individual responsibility and empowerment
highlights the closing quotation by Jambeck (l. 38-42) as the rhetorical climax that frames individual choices as impactful

options.label: 3a — Comment ("your choices can make an impact")

criteria.short: Bezieht klar Stellung zu Mosbergens These "your choices can make an impact"
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling bezieht klar Stellung zu Mosbergens These "your choices can make an impact", z. B.:
bullets: takes a clear stance on whether individual choices can genuinely make a difference to ocean pollution
formulates a precise thesis statement early in the comment
differentiates between agreeing, partially agreeing or disagreeing with the statement, avoiding a vague or purely descriptive stance
considers the statement in relation to both individual and systemic responsibility
supports the chosen position consistently with matching arguments throughout

criteria.short: Begründet seine Position durch nachvollziehbare Argumente
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling begründet seine Position durch nachvollziehbare Argumente, z. B.:
bullets: supports the stance with logical, well-developed arguments rather than mere assertions
weighs the potential impact of individual action against systemic factors such as industry and policy
addresses possible counterarguments (e.g. that individual choices are too small-scale to matter) and responds to them
uses examples to illustrate how individual behaviour can or cannot influence larger environmental outcomes
draws a reasoned conclusion that follows logically from the arguments presented

criteria.short: Bezieht im Unterricht behandelte Inhalte konkret in seine Argumentation ein
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling bezieht im Unterricht behandelte Inhalte konkret in seine Argumentation ein, z. B.:
bullets: draws on classroom knowledge about global warming to support or qualify the claim that individual choices matter
refers to what was learned about supply chains to assess how much influence individual consumers actually have
uses knowledge about (plastic) pollution more broadly to contextualise Mosbergen's statement
connects at least one of these class topics explicitly and by name to the argument being made
shows how the connection to class content strengthens or complicates the position taken

criteria.short: Stützt seine Argumentation durch persönliche Erfahrungen
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling stützt seine Argumentation durch persönliche Erfahrungen, z. B.:
bullets: includes at least one concrete personal example related to plastic use or environmental behaviour
explains how this personal experience relates to the wider claim about individual impact
reflects critically on the limits or effectiveness of their own everyday choices
integrates the personal example coherently into the overall argument rather than adding it as an afterthought

criteria.short: Eröffnet den Leserbrief mit einem klaren Bezug zu Mosbergens Artikel und formuliert sein Anliegen
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling eröffnet den Leserbrief mit einem klaren Bezug zu Mosbergens Artikel und formuliert sein Anliegen, z. B.:
bullets: opens the letter with a clear reference to Mosbergen's article and its central claim
states the purpose of writing (e.g. reacting to the claim about individual impact) early and explicitly
addresses the readership of the newspaper appropriately as a letter to the editor
establishes the writer's perspective as an interested, environmentally engaged high-school student
identifies the specific claim from the article that the writer intends to respond to, setting up the following argument

criteria.short: Entwickelt eine eigene, begründete Position zur Rolle des Einzelnen
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling entwickelt eine eigene, begründete Position zur Rolle des Einzelnen, z. B.:
bullets: takes and maintains a clear position on whether individual choices can make a meaningful impact
develops arguments that support this position in a logical sequence
considers the role of young people/students specifically in shaping future environmental outcomes
addresses a possible counter-perspective (e.g. scepticism about individual impact) within the letter
concludes with a call to action or a clear closing statement addressed to fellow readers

criteria.short: Bezieht im Unterricht behandelte Inhalte konkret in den Leserbrief ein
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling bezieht im Unterricht behandelte Inhalte konkret in den Leserbrief ein, z. B.:
bullets: draws on classroom knowledge about global warming to underline the urgency of the issue
refers to what was learned about supply chains to discuss the limits or potential of individual consumer choices
uses knowledge about (plastic) pollution more broadly to support the letter's argument
names at least one of these class topics explicitly within the letter
integrates the class-based knowledge naturally into the voice and purpose of a letter to the editor

criteria.short: Stützt den Leserbrief durch persönliche Erfahrungen
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling stützt den Leserbrief durch persönliche Erfahrungen, z. B.:
bullets: includes at least one concrete personal example related to environmental behaviour or activism
relates this personal experience convincingly to the letter's overall message
reflects on what this experience suggests about the potential of individual action
integrates the personal example in a way that fits the tone and purpose of a letter to the editor

criteria.short: Richtet seinen Text konsequent und explizit im Sinne der Aufgabenstellung auf die Intention und den Adressaten aus
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling richtet seinen Text konsequent und explizit im Sinne der Aufgabenstellung auf die Intention und den Adressaten aus.
